action: Trace surveyor deployment and its geometry budget
observation: The machine layer casts this surveyor at the Helios unanswered survey, Veil survey monolith and Ashfall maintenance scene. Its current builder has five meshes, five per-machine materials and five geometries shared across machines, totaling 648 triangles per root and 18448 unique typed-array bytes. The emissive torus alone contributes 480 triangles; the faceted body has eight. Its scan arm deployment reads the worker-published winding boolean or the in-process sweep threshold.
decision: Do not reduce the ring or replace the faceted body from counts alone: inspect the deployed/stowed silhouette and nacre material at the real gameplay camera first, then compare any lower-segment ring against it.
next: Capture an identified surveyor at its Helios or Veil site in quiet and scan-winding states, and compare its ring against a lower-segment candidate if visibly equivalent.
evidenceScope: Source route and Node-built resource census with mock-loaded skin; not an on-screen appearance, actual draw count, worker-route acceptance or performance measurement.
performance: The ring represents 480 of 648 per-root triangles and is a potential optimization target; no GPU timing or game FPS claim.

action: Trace the scanner's enclosed pupil and motion
observation: The builder places the luminous pupil at the same center as an opaque, depth-writing octahedral body. In both sampled stowed and scanning poses every pupil vertex lies strictly inside that body, with a maximum normalized octahedral radius of about 0.271; the work animation moves only the external tool arm. The ordinary site-cast machine has no explicit light metadata and resolves to no Nocturne archetype.
decision: Compare visible output, actual submitted draws and an exposed-pupil study in the current renderer before changing the enclosed object. An exposed light may be useful design, while simply deleting an intended detail would be premature.
next: Inspect the in-flight matched Helios and Veil comparisons and check any other route-specific light ownership.
evidenceScope: Node geometry containment and source trace; it does not establish rendered pixel equality, all possible explicit light metadata or live FPS.
performance: The enclosed sphere is 140 submitted triangles if drawn and has its own material; actual draw submission and frame impact are not yet measured.

action: Compare the enclosed pupil and a visible scanner study
observation: With the same Veil chase and side camera, pose, recorded light state and current renderer ownership, hiding the centered pupil produced pixel-identical images. The instrumented presented pass submitted that pupil once per frame when enabled and zero times when hidden across the 15-frame samples. Moving the sphere onto the face made a large bright disc that read as an applied sticker rather than integrated instrumentation.
decision: Remove the invisible enclosed pupil and preserve the exposed-scanner idea as a separate authored body/tool study rather than shipping the large luminous disc. Keep the existing 40-segment ring until a smaller candidate preserves its silhouette.
next: Check live scanner motion and material lifetime after the narrow removal, and hand off the instrument geometry brief to Astra.
evidenceScope: Target-isolated held Veil views after diagnostic relocation; screenshots, owner checks and guarded submitted-draw counters are recorded. Helios top background changed and the Helios side observation had an FOV difference, so those are not used as exact comparisons. This is not ordinary play or whole-game frame timing.
performance: The tested visible machine drops from five to four mesh submissions per sampled presented frame and 648 to 508 triangles per root when the 140-triangle pupil is removed. Per-instance material objects drop from five to four. No FPS or frame-time claim.

observation: The same-session 4-by-24-segment torus is visibly angular in the matched Veil chase and close side frames compared with the existing 6-by-40 ring. Its cross section is also coarser. Both preserve the same radius and material.
decision: Reject this 4-by-24 candidate and retain the current ring; a smaller quality-preserving segment reduction can be compared separately.
next: Test a smaller adjustment that preserves the circular silhouette, alongside material alternatives, before changing the shared cached ring geometry.
evidenceScope: Current renderer with target isolated after a diagnostic relocation, held camera, pose and recorded light state. No ordinary encounter or live frame-time comparison.
performance: The scratch ring has 192 rather than 480 triangles and 5152 bytes of typed arrays; this is a geometry budget comparison, not a measured FPS gain.

action: Compare the nacre relief strength on the current body
observation: In the matched Veil side view, the current full-strength normal map reads as crumpled, highly reflective foil. Reducing its strength to 0.3 keeps some relief while reducing harsh highlights. Removing the normal map produces a calmer surface while retaining the existing nacre albedo and its panel pattern.
decision: Keep both softer and albedo-only treatments as scratch options. The pending authored body may alter the UVs and facets, so defer the production material choice until it is reviewed on that form.
next: Compare both treatments on the authored body under the same lighting and useful chase scale; avoid a separate new texture unless it materially improves the result.
evidenceScope: Current-renderer isolated Veil side view after diagnostic relocation; camera, lighting, owner and sampled background match, and all three variants submit the body. Helios background changed and later Veil chase variants stopped drawing, so they do not establish this comparison.
performance: The albedo-only shader omits a normal-map sample on this body, but the shared normal texture remains used by other machines. No GPU time or FPS improvement was measured.

observation: The four-radial, forty-circumference candidate retains the existing ring outline in the matched Veil close side view. The two 32-circumference alternatives show more faceting. The 4-by-40 candidate's Veil chase frame stopped drawing and the Helios chase frame was clipped, so neither establishes its gameplay-scale outline.
decision: Keep 4-by-40 as a scratch candidate but preserve the existing ring until a valid matching chase comparison accompanies the close view.
next: Compare the candidate against the current ring in a fully framed chase view, ideally alongside the forthcoming authored body study.
evidenceScope: Current-renderer target-isolated Veil close view after diagnostic relocation; camera, pose, recorded lighting and sampled background match. The invalid or clipped chase frames are documented in the comparison report.
performance: 4-by-40 uses 320 instead of 480 triangles and 8480 instead of 12064 shared typed-array bytes; both variants retain one ring mesh. No frame-time or FPS comparison.

observation: The renderer supplies an absolute authored clock, but the shared machine motion helper previously used that value as a delta as well. At time 100 seconds, a stowed Surveyor's first scan update jumped directly to its fully deployed pitch; an explicit 16 ms delta produced the intended intermediate pitch. Seven machine builders use the helper.
decision: Derive delta from successive absolute timestamps, initialize newly admitted machines at their actual work state, and preserve the supported explicit and default delta call forms. Equal or backward absolute clocks cause no artificial motion. The old immediate-restow assertion was updated to verify easing and eventual rest.
next: Observe a naturally cycling Helios Surveyor through the renderer to verify multiple intermediate updates; do not claim the Node result as ordinary-play motion.
evidenceScope: Renderer and helper source trace, focused Node reproduction and tests, with the shipping fix committed as c7f3923183e6. A real rendered transition is pending.
performance: The fix adds only per-machine scalar clock state and arithmetic; no live timing or FPS measurement.

action: Check the Astra Surveyor body, scanner arm and optical rim against the existing builder and motion contract.
observation: The scratch geometry has finite attributes, nondegenerate UVs and outward winding; the existing ring, four mesh/material identities, transforms and work-motion behavior remain intact. Its replacement body and scanner use 408 triangles versus 28 before.
decision: Keep it as a candidate rather than accepting a triangle increase without seeing the actual renderer.
next: Compare the new shape and normal strength at multiple views.
evidenceScope: Scratch geometry and focused procedural-owner checks; not a player route.
performance: The candidate adds 380 triangles and 39168 shared typed-array bytes before any ring reduction; no measured frame-time change.

action: Compare the candidate shape, three normal treatments and the four-sided ring in twenty current-renderer diagnostic views.
observation: Every view submitted the same four target meshes. The faceted housing and scanner read more deliberately constructed, while 0.3 normal strength reduces the foil-like highlights and retains nacre detail. The 4-by-40 ring keeps a similar outline at the sampled chase view. Exposure drifted slightly as the preview settled, so these images are not a matched color or timing measurement.
decision: Prefer the softened candidate and hold it for a live-scene comparison in both actual Surveyor locations before modifying production.
next: Inspect deployed and stowed scanner poses and the ring under the two sector light rigs.
evidenceScope: Current FleetLook diagnostic with runtime skins; no ordinary encounter.
performance: With the 4-by-40 ring the candidate totals 728 versus 508 baseline triangles, with the same four isolated submissions; no gameplay FPS measurement.

action: Compare the faceted scanner candidate in the live Helios and Veil scenes after diagnostic relocation.
observation: The candidate has a more deliberate inset shell and optical housing under both sector lighting rigs. Three views captured each of three material/geometry options, with four target submissions per frame; the Helios chase framing timed out and some separate projection diagnostics disagreed with the visible inspection-camera images.
decision: Retain the softer nacre response and lower-section ring for the production trial; do not claim a normal unassisted encounter or a complete chase comparison.
next: Verify the actual production geometry and existing work motion through the renderer.
evidenceScope: Launched New Game followed by diagnostic sector relocation, isolated layers and held poses; not ordinary encounter acceptance.
performance: Four observed target submissions in each sampled frame; no matched frame-time result.

action: Install the reviewed shared geometry and inspect its actual production builder from four views.
observation: The shell, scanner and ring load with four visible target draws. The new shared body/arm/tip carry 408 triangles, while reducing the ring from 480 to 320; the original total was 508 triangles and the new total is 728.
decision: Keep the increased geometric detail and softer normal response while sharing all geometry between instances.
next: Continue the remaining asset iterations and verify an ordinary encounter and measured frame time when available.
evidenceScope: Current production-builder FleetLook views and focused motion/lifetime tests.
performance: 220 additional triangles per visible prism, no added target draws, about 39 KB of shared attribute data for new parts; no gameplay FPS claim.
